title: Media Player's "Media volume up/down" shortcuts should respect the system's volume stepping setting
line: The Media volume up/down shortcuts now change a player's volume by the volume step set in the audio settings instead of always 5%.
explanation: The Media Controller global shortcuts are handled by the mprisservice kded module, which called changeVolume(±0.05) with a hardcoded 5% step. The Media Player widget's wheel already used the [General] VolumeStep from plasmaparc, so the two behaved differently when the user changed the step. The module now keeps a KConfigWatcher on plasmaparc and uses VolumeStep/100 (default 5) for both shortcuts, so changes in System Settings apply immediately.

commits.message:
libkmpris/kded: use the system volume step for media volume shortcuts

The "Media volume up" and "Media volume down" global shortcuts always
changed the player's volume by 5%, ignoring the volume step set in the
audio settings. They now read that step, like the Media Player widget.

BUG: 505557

media.caption: Volume step set to 15%, player at 50%, Media volume up pressed twice: the player only reaches 60% (5% steps).
Same steps with the fix: the player reaches 80% (15% steps).

reviews.text: Straightforward, idiomatic fix in libkmpris's kded module that watches plasmaparc via KConfigWatcher and reads [General] VolumeStep (default 5) to match the Media Player widget. Live config changes apply without restarting kded6, and deleting the key falls back cleanly to 5%. Screenshots, verification steps, and commit message are accurate and complete.

Exactly the change Nate agreed to in c1: the mprisservice kded module now uses plasmaparc [General] VolumeStep (default 5) instead of the hardcoded 0.05, reading it the same way the Media Player widget's GlobalConfig does, so shortcuts and wheel agree. KConfigWatcher reparses on notify, so a change in System Settings applies without restarting kded (verified with --notify), and the ConfigCore link is correct. Evidence (0.55/0.60 before vs 0.65/0.80 after with step 15, OSD at 80%) and the commit text match the small patch.
